props.title: Growth vs. Activation Trade-off
props.summary: While top-of-funnel acquisition successfully drove weekly active users up by 33%, the onboarding experience struggled to keep pace, resulting in a 5% slip in user activation.

blocks.note: Weekly active users grew significantly, but onboarding efficiency dropped during the surge.
Retention remains highly stable at 58%, indicating that users who do activate find long-term value.

props.title: Feature Adoption Rates
props.footer: Core utility features lead, while the new dashboard remains in early single-digit adoption.

blocks.note: Search is your most utilized feature at 71%, while the new dashboard sits at a low 18% adoption.
blocks.noteSpoken: Search is your most utilized feature at seventy-one percent, while the new dashboard sits at a low eighteen percent adoption.

props.recommendation: Prioritize activation flow optimization to prevent the growing top-of-funnel traffic from leaking out early.

blocks.note: The middle of your funnel is the primary leak point, as acquisition and retention are both performing well.

frames.question: Walk me through the funnel: 60k signups, 21.6k activated, 12.5k still active after 30 days, and 3.1k on a paid plan.
frames.narration: The biggest drop in your funnel occurs at the very first step, where 64% of signups fail to activate, resulting in 21,600 activated users from your 60,000 total signups.
frames.spoken: The biggest drop in your funnel occurs at the very first step, where sixty-four percent of signups fail to activate, resulting in twenty-one thousand six hundred activated users from your sixty thousand total signups.

tour.say: Our primary concern this quarter is the activation rate, which slipped five percent down to thirty-six percent.
When we look at the math, the step from signup to activation is where we lose sixty-four percent of our users.
This bottleneck is likely related to feature adoption, where the new dashboard is only reaching eighteen percent of users.
